description: Unit-cost Levenshtein distance on run-length encoded strings using run-pair DP blocks and boundary propagation.

source.title: Similarity Between Compressed Strings
source.algorithm_attribution: Run-length encoded Levenshtein distance by extending run-pair block computation with unit insertion, deletion, and substitution costs.
source.implementation_status: clean-room bounded profile; no chapter prose or cited-paper code copied

workspace.meaning: At most four run-block boundary rows/columns and temporary state for one block.

contract.block_layout: One dynamic-programming block is formed for every pair of left and right runs.
contract.block_recurrence: Each cell is the minimum of deletion from above plus one, insertion from the left plus one, and diagonal substitution with cost zero for equal symbols or one otherwise.
contract.boundary_initialization: The top boundary stores the right-string prefix length and the left boundary stores the left-string prefix length.
contract.boundary_propagation: Each block consumes its top and left boundaries, then passes its bottom and right boundaries to adjacent blocks.
contract.input_representation: Ports retain run symbols and lengths and never materialize the expanded strings.
contract.result: The lower-right dynamic-programming value is returned; no edit script is selected.

oracle_method: The primary oracle propagates run-pair block boundaries. The independent verifier evaluates the full unit-cost edit-distance table while reading each symbol from its encoded run sequence on demand.
